newsitem.title: USA: CME LIVE CATTLE SEEN STEADY TO OFF, FEEDERS LOWER.
newsitem.headline: CME LIVE CATTLE SEEN STEADY TO OFF, FEEDERS LOWER.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent per lb lower while feeder cattle futures were called 0.500 to 1.000 cent lower, livestock analysts said.
Although cash live cattle markets were expected to remain firm, the continued weakness in boxed beef items will likely weigh on live cattle futures, traders said.
The beef market has remained on the defensive despite expectations of increased demand for the Labor Day holiday. Spillover weakness from feeder cattle futures is also likely, they said.

Carryover selling from Tuesday's limit losses and further advances in corn futures were expected to keep feeder cattle pressured. Concern over feed costs will keep demand for feeder cattle thin, they said.
Anticipation of Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed Report may influence trading with the July placement figure likely to be the most closely watched number.

Early placement estimates for the major seven states averaged 100.8 percent and ranged from 96 to 106.5 percent of a year ago. On-feed estimates averaged 115.6 percent and ranged between 114 to 117.8 percent, and marketings averaged 105.5 percent on a range of 103 to 107 percent of a year ago.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.11 at $81.39 per cwt.
